generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and sport science, progressing follows the same loop. A disappointing result in a biomechanics assessment, or a skill you cannot yet perform, becomes information about what to work on next. That feeds the self-belief to keep practising and a mastery goal, such as understanding movement analysis, that lasts beyond one test.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport-science students find the physiology module hard. One reads a poor mark on an early assignment as proof the subject is not for them, and aims only to pass. The other treats it as information, builds confidence by mastering one body system at a time, and sets a goal to understand how the body responds to training, not just to clear the exam. By the end of the module, the second student applies physiology with confidence, in study and in coaching.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and sport science, the three habits work best as one continuing practice. You read a setback in training or study as information, build the self-belief and learning motivation to keep going, and set a mastery goal that builds lasting capability. Running that loop, module after module, is what moves you forward.

check.body: A student gets a poor mark on an early essay. They read the feedback as showing what to work on, build their confidence by improving one weak area at a time, and set a goal to get better at structuring an argument. By the end of term their essays are stronger. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three habits worked as one practice: a growth response, self-belief and learning motivation, and a mastery goal, each feeding the next across the term.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three ran together, round after round, and the work improved.

_items.text: That the first poor mark was a fair verdict on their ability.
_items.feedback: The point is the opposite: the student treated the mark as information, not a verdict.

_items.text: That only the final essay mark matters, not what came before it.
_items.feedback: What came before is the point. The habits across the term made the later work stronger.

_items.text: That setting a goal alone was enough, with no change in mindset or effort.
_items.feedback: The goal worked because a growth response and real effort sat behind it.
